## Judgment

### Expected-drift set

Three commits land in this range, each with its own registry key or input.

- `b05f212` (drop gtk-engine-murrine) touches `modules/user/home.nix`, key
  `user-home`. `consumers.sh user-home` resolves to sweet16 and petunia only
  (`hosts/sweet16/home.nix`, `hosts/petunia/home.nix`).
- `d0c071a` (bump nixpkgs-unstable, lock-diff.sh: `0954f7e` → `6774f7b`, the
  only node that moved) is consumed two ways: directly, wherever a module
  reaches `inputs.nixpkgs-unstable` (`consumers.sh nixpkgs-unstable` →
  sweet16, petunia, hermes, dualie, forge, rk3588); and transitively through
  `herdr`, whose `flake.nix` entry sets `inputs.nixpkgs.follows =
  "nixpkgs-unstable"`. `consumers.sh herdr` resolves to all seven configs
  (sweet16, petunia, avina, hermes, dualie, forge, rk3588 — every
  `user-herdr-home` consumer, including `hosts/avina/home.nix`). Taking the
  union of both queries, every config in the fleet is an expected consumer
  of this bump.
- `a3ad2ba` (core-printing 26.11 gate) touches key `core-printing`.
  `consumers.sh core-printing` resolves to sweet16 and petunia only
  (`hosts/sweet16/default.nix`, `hosts/petunia/default.nix`). The new branch
  is gated on `lib.versionAtLeast lib.trivial.release "26.11"`; sweet16
  builds against nixpkgs 26.05 so it stays on the pre-existing
  `ensure-printers.service` branch (verified byte-identical to the
  pre-refactor `systemd.services` block, just re-wrapped in
  `lib.mkIf (!newProvisioning)`), petunia builds against nixpkgs-unstable
  (currently 26.11) and picks up the new `cups.service` shape.

Union across all three commits, excluding `groot@rk3588` (N/A on x86_64 per
the pipeline contract): sweet16, petunia, avina, hermes, groot@dualie,
groot@forge all expected to drift.

### Actual vs expected

`verify-drift.sh 8e6c54b a3ad2ba` (exit 10, drift found) reports DRIFT for
sweet16, petunia, avina, hermes, groot@dualie, groot@forge, and N/A for
groot@rk3588. This is an exact match against the expected-drift set above.

avina is not a direct consumer of the literal `nixpkgs-unstable` string
(`consumers.sh nixpkgs-unstable` alone does not list it), so a first pass
looked like a mismatch. I traced avina's drifted toplevel derivation by hand
(`nix derivation show` on the toplevel .drv, then its `etc.drv` input, then
the differing `user-environment.drv` input, then its `home-manager-path.drv`
input) and found the only substantive difference is the `herdr-0.9.0.drv`
input hash. avina reaches `herdr` through
`hosts/avina/home.nix` (`avina-home`) → `homeManagerModules.user-herdr-home`
→ `inputs.herdr.packages.${system}.herdr`, and `herdr`'s own flake input
`nixpkgs` follows `nixpkgs-unstable` (see `flake.nix`, `herdr.inputs.nixpkgs.follows
= "nixpkgs-unstable"`). `consumers.sh` is a static grep over literal
`inputs.<name>` references; it cannot walk a `follows` edge declared inside
a nested flake input, so it does not surface `herdr` as a consumer of
`nixpkgs-unstable` on its own. Re-running it with `herdr` as an explicit
second query name resolves to all seven configs and accounts for avina (and
confirms the other nixpkgs-unstable-driven hosts independently). With that
addition the expected and actual sets are equal — the sets genuinely match,
the gap was in the query, not in the drift.

Petunia's drift also carries the `stdenv.isLinux`/`stdenv.isDarwin`
deprecated evaluation warning from `nix flake check --impure`, confirmed
present only for `nixosConfigurations.petunia` and absent for sweet16/avina/
hermes. `grep -rn 'stdenv\.isLinux\|stdenv\.isDarwin' modules/ hosts/
profiles/ lib/` returns no hits, confirming it originates in nixpkgs-unstable
internals (pulled in transitively, likely through the herdr/rust-overlay or
another unstable-only package expression), not our own code. I judge this
should NOT be added to the AGENTS.md §10 known-warnings list: that list
documents warnings that are structurally permanent given this repo's fixed
tooling choices (devenv 2.2.0, the `modules` flake output, the
`aarch64-linux` systems declaration). This warning is an artifact of the
current nixpkgs-unstable pin and is likely to change or disappear on a
future `nixpkgs-unstable` bump once upstream finishes its own
`stdenv.hostPlatform.isLinux` migration — it is not a fixed property of
nix-nexus's own code or tooling the way the four canonical warnings are.
